authority_boundary.purpose: Source acquisition, provenance, chronology, objective textual relationships, physical-evidence inputs, and nuclear-material statement inventory only.

source_chronology.originating_source: Atomic Energy Organization of Iran head Mohammad Eslami
source_chronology.proposition: Eslami said removal of enriched uranium from Iran was not on the agenda; the article also described an approximately 400 kg pre-strike stock of 60%-enriched uranium.
source_chronology.bounded_excerpt: Such a matter has fundamentally not been on the agenda.

source_chronology.proposition: Reuters reported that an IAEA report placed uranium enriched to 20% and 60% at the Isfahan tunnel complex immediately before the war.
Reuters reported Grossi saying a little over 200 kg of 60%-enriched uranium had been at Isfahan and was likely still there.

source_chronology.originating_source: Press TV analysis by Yousef Ramazani
source_chronology.proposition: Press TV described a hypothetical operation to seize Iran's enriched-uranium stockpile as requiring a brigade-sized perimeter force, sustained air cover, ISR, logistics, packaging, transport, and specialized handling.
source_chronology.bounded_excerpt: Approximately 1,000 pounds of 60 percent highly enriched uranium would need to be packaged, moved, and transported to a secure location.

source_chronology.originating_source: U.S. officials and former defense/special-operations officials
source_chronology.proposition: The Post reported a separate U.S. contingency plan to seize nearly 1,000 pounds of enriched uranium, involving excavation equipment, substantial forces, a runway/cargo-aircraft solution, and an operation potentially lasting weeks.
Press TV acknowledged Iran's increased uranium enrichment while distinguishing it from weapons-grade material and reiterating Iran's peaceful-program position.
source_chronology.bounded_excerpt: Iran was forced to ramp up its uranium enrichment, but it remains nowhere close to weapons-grade.

source_chronology.originating_source: IRGC / Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters as reported by Press TV
source_chronology.proposition: Press TV reported the downed aircraft as a second F-35 and described the pilot's fate as unknown because of the aircraft's destruction.
Tasnim reported that the missing U.S. airman may have been captured and attributed the possibility to unspecified sources.
Tasnim's headline said the U.S. recovery effort failed while the body qualified that recovery efforts had so far been futile.
Iran International reported a provincial IRGC denial that the second F-15 crew member had been captured or detained.

source_chronology.originating_source: Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters spokesman Lt. Col. Ebrahim Zolfaqari
source_chronology.proposition: Press TV reported that Iranian forces destroyed two C-130 transport planes and two Black Hawk helicopters during a mission described as retrieving the downed U.S. pilot; the spokesman characterized the operation as a complete failure.
source_chronology.bounded_excerpt: two C-130 military transport planes and two Black Hawk helicopters were destroyed

source_chronology.originating_source: Iranian unified command, Iranian army and IRGC statements; U.S. officials
source_chronology.proposition: Reuters reported the Iranian claim that two C-130s and two Black Hawks were destroyed by Iranian forces and also reported U.S. officials saying the second F-15E airman had been rescued.
CENTCOM stated that two U.S. service members from the downed F-15E were safely recovered in separate search-and-rescue missions.
source_chronology.bounded_excerpt: successfully completed the rescues of two American service members from Iran

source_chronology.originating_source: U.S. officials and sources familiar with the operation
source_chronology.proposition: Reuters reported that two MC-130 aircraft became unable to take off, the rescue force was extracted in stages, and U.S. troops destroyed the disabled MC-130s and four additional helicopters rather than leave sensitive equipment.
Press TV identified the wreckage as F-15E rather than the F-35 identification carried in earlier Iranian reporting.

source_chronology.originating_source: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei
source_chronology.proposition: Xinhua reported Baghaei raising the possibility that the rescue explanation could have been a deception connected to stealing enriched uranium.

source_chronology.originating_source: U.S. officials including President Trump, Gen. Dan Caine and CIA Director John Ratcliffe
source_chronology.proposition: AP reported a two-stage rescue using dozens of aircraft and hundreds of personnel; cargo aircraft and helicopters were left behind or destroyed after the second recovery.

source_chronology.originating_source: Press TV exclusive information; unnamed/highly placed Tehran source also quoted
source_chronology.proposition: Press TV stated that the Isfahan operation was unrelated to the F-15 rescue and that its objective was to infiltrate and attack an Isfahan nuclear facility; the same article said U.S. forces later evacuated personnel and bombed their own abandoned equipment.
epistemic_terms: evidence examined and confirmed by Press TV
source_chronology.bounded_excerpt: this operation had no connection to the claimed rescue ... the real objective was to infiltrate and attack one of Iran's nuclear facilities

source_chronology.proposition: Molaei's article questioned the rescue account, described a larger operation and possibly undisclosed objectives, and acknowledged reporting that U.S. forces destroyed stranded equipment themselves.
epistemic_terms: had there been any other operation
source_chronology.bounded_excerpt: This suggests a larger operation, and possibly undisclosed objectives.
source_chronology.attribution_note: The page states that the views expressed do not necessarily reflect Press TV.

provenance_relationships.basis: Possible-capture reporting is followed by a reported provincial IRGC denial of capture/detention.
Early failed-recovery framing and later official U.S. statement of two successful recoveries describe different rescue outcomes.
Complete-failure characterization conflicts textually with CENTCOM's successful-recovery statement.
Press TV attributed destruction of rescue transports/helicopters to Iranian forces; Reuters reported disabled aircraft/equipment were destroyed by U.S. troops.
April 5 reporting described a mission to retrieve the downed pilot; April 7 Press TV said the operation had no connection to that rescue.
Both reports attribute the uranium/deception possibility to Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei.
The April 9 analysis embeds/references the April 7 Press TV exclusive while using more hedged language about additional objectives.
Press TV later identified the earlier F-35 identification as a misidentification and identified the debris as F-15E.
Both Reuters reports relay IAEA information concerning 60%-enriched uranium at Isfahan.
Press TV published operational requirements for a hypothetical uranium-seizure mission before its April 7 Isfahan mission-purpose report.
The Post documented a separate U.S. uranium-seizure contingency plan before the April 7 Press TV claim; no source relationship establishes that the contingency plan was executed in the rescue.

source_family_connections.basis: Press TV directly quotes spokesman Ebrahim Zolfaqari.

source_family_connections.connected_entity: Unified command of Iranian armed forces / Iranian Army / IRGC
source_family_connections.basis: Reuters attributes specific aircraft-loss claims to those institutions.
Xinhua attributes the uranium/deception possibility to Baghaei.
Anadolu carries the same official statement family.
The article repeatedly describes information/evidence as obtained, examined, or confirmed by Press TV; underlying sourcing is partly unnamed.
Named analyst byline; page includes an outlet disclaimer separating the author's views from Press TV.
Tasnim presents capture as a possibility attributed to unspecified sources.

correction_update_language.note: Press TV identifies the earlier F-35 identification as a misidentification.
The April 7 article says the operation had no connection to the claimed F-15 rescue while linking to the April 5 feature; it does not label the earlier Press TV rescue-purpose report a correction.
The April 9 article uses possibility language and includes an author-view disclaimer.

physical_evidence_inventory.description: Official U.S. statement that both F-15E service members were safely recovered in separate search-and-rescue missions.
Reuters reconstruction reporting two MC-130 aircraft unable to take off and U.S. destruction of the disabled transports and four additional helicopters before extraction.
AP reconstruction reporting dozens of aircraft, hundreds of personnel, delivery of small helicopters by cargo aircraft, and destruction of equipment left on the ground.
Press TV April 7 description of C-130s, special forces, specialized vehicles, MH-6 helicopters and later U.S. bombing of abandoned equipment.
Press TV April 9 analysis describes HC-130 aircraft on the ground, unloaded light helicopters and U.S. destruction of stranded assets as reported by American media.
Pre-event Press TV analysis stated a uranium-seizure mission would require a 3,000-4,000-person perimeter force, sustained air cover, ISR, extended logistics and specialized handling.

Pre-event Washington Post reporting on a separate uranium-seizure contingency plan described excavation equipment, runway/cargo-aircraft requirements, radiological protection and a weeks-scale operation.

nuclear_material_statement_inventory.statement: AEOI chief Mohammad Eslami said removal of enriched uranium from Iran was not on the agenda and linked possible dilution of 60% material to sanctions relief; Press TV described about 400 kg of highly enriched uranium before the prior strikes.
Reuters reported an IAEA report stating that uranium enriched to 20% and 60% had been stored at the Isfahan tunnel complex immediately before the war.
Reuters reported Grossi saying a little over 200 kg of Iran's 60%-enriched uranium had been at Isfahan and likely remained there.
Press TV's hypothetical seizure analysis described approximately 1,000 pounds of 60%-enriched uranium, Natanz/Isfahan as secured locations, and specialized handling/transport requirements.

The Washington Post reported a U.S. contingency plan concerning nearly 1,000 pounds of 60%-enriched uranium, with more than half described as stored outside Isfahan and the remainder at Natanz or other locations.
Press TV acknowledged increased Iranian enrichment while expressly distinguishing the material from weapons-grade and reiterating Iran's peaceful-program position.

scope: other foreign/social-media citations directly connected to CH-F15E-CSAR-URANIUM
method: Repository text search for the named accounts
Targeted Press TV domain searches for the named accounts and F-15E/Isfahan context
external_commentary_feedback_review.limitation: This records the reviewed source universe only; it is not a claim that no such citation exists anywhere outside the reviewed corpus.

unresolved_provenance_gaps.description: A first-party Iranian Foreign Ministry publication or transcript for Baghaei's April 6 uranium/deception remarks was not recovered in the reviewed corpus; Xinhua and Anadolu are retained as parallel carriers.

The underlying sources for Press TV's April 7 'information obtained' and 'evidence examined and confirmed' language are not fully identified; the article also quotes an unnamed highly placed Tehran source.
Several Press TV and Tasnim pages expose clock times without an explicit timezone on the page; those times are preserved as source-display times and are not converted.
Embedded social-media imagery associated with the rescue-equipment wreckage is not separately canonicalized here when the underlying image origin cannot be independently identified.
No chain-relevant feedback path involving the specifically named foreign social-media accounts was identified in the current repository or targeted Press TV search.
The reviewed record does not contain an independently verified coordinate-level geolocation of the abandoned airstrip tied to the April 7 nuclear-site assertion.

downstream_handoff.note: This artifact records sources, provenance, wording, chronology, textual conflicts, source-family links and physical/nuclear-material inputs. It makes no downstream analytical finding.
